Outside the book's StdIn library, standard Java reads keyboard input with java.util.Scanner (nextInt(), nextDouble(), nextLine()); a token of the wrong type stops the program with InputMismatchException.

When execution reaches a read, the program blocks until a complete token is available (at the terminal, until <return>). The read then parses the token and returns, the assignment stores the value, and the next statement runs.
